issue: No service layer: controllers call Mongoose models directly. Business logic (order creation, paid/delivered transitions, review aggregation, feature-flag mutation) lives inside Express request handlers, mixing HTTP concerns with domain logic. This is consistent across all controllers (order, product, user, featureFlag), making logic untestable without HTTP and unreusable across entry points (e.g. the MCP servers cannot reuse it).
evidence: addOrderItems/updateOrderToPaid build & save Order documents inline; createProductReview computes numReviews + rating average inline in productController.js:137-141
recommendation: Introduce a service layer (OrderService, ProductService, etc.) holding domain logic; controllers become thin HTTP adapters. Document the layering choice (controller -> service -> model) in a new ADR. Given the small size this is C2, not a blocker, but it is the root cause of several findings below.

issue: Server trusts client-computed money. addOrderItems persists itemsPrice/taxPrice/shippingPrice/totalPrice exactly as sent by the client; the values are computed in the frontend (PlaceOrderScreen.jsx:23-28, 15% tax, $100 shipping threshold). Pricing/tax/shipping is core domain logic that lives entirely in the presentation layer and is never recomputed or validated server-side. A client can submit any totalPrice.
evidence: PlaceOrderScreen.jsx:27 cart.taxPrice = addDecimals(Number((0.15 * cart.itemsPrice).toFixed(2))); -> orderActions.createOrder POSTs those fields -> orderController addOrderItems stores them verbatim
recommendation: Move price/tax/shipping calculation server-side (a pricing service or model method) using authoritative product prices from the DB; treat client-sent totals as untrusted. Compounds ADR-0002's payment-trust gap. Propose ADR documenting server-authoritative order pricing.

issue: Feature-flag store is a flat JSON file (backend/features.json) accessed by direct fs.readFileSync/writeFileSync from TWO independent processes: the Express backend controller AND the feature-flags MCP server (mcp-server-feature-flags/src/index.ts:28-35). Both read-modify-write the same file with no locking, no transaction, no shared abstraction. Concurrent writes (admin UI PUT + MCP set_feature_state) can silently clobber each other (lost update / last-writer-wins).
evidence: featureFlagController.js writeFileSync(FEATURES_PATH,...) at line 70; mcp-server-feature-flags/src/index.ts saveFeatures() at line 33; docker-compose.yml:23 and :53 bind-mount the same file into both containers
recommendation: Define a single owner of the feature-flag store behind one interface (a shared module or a small HTTP API the MCP calls). Add a write lock or move to a transactional store. Document the file-as-database decision and its single-writer constraint in a new ADR.

issue: The feature-flag MCP server re-implements the same domain rules as the backend controller (load/validate/mutate flags) with DIVERGENT contracts: the MCP allows status 'Shadow' and enforces dependency/traffic guards (cannot enable if a dependency is Disabled; cannot set traffic>0 while Disabled); the backend controller (featureFlagController.js:51) only allows Enabled|Testing|Disabled and has NONE of those guards. The two writers to the same file disagree on what a valid state is.
evidence: MCP enum Enabled|Disabled|Testing|Shadow (index.ts:18) + dependency guard (index.ts:185-202); backend allows only ['Enabled','Testing','Disabled'] (featureFlagController.js:51) with no dependency/traffic checks
recommendation: Extract a single shared feature-flag domain module (validation + dependency rules) consumed by both the controller and the MCP server, or make one the sole writer and the other a thin client. Eliminates contract drift.

issue: Three distinct persistence technologies now exist: MongoDB (orders/users/products), a JSON file (feature flags), and PostgreSQL+pgvector (RAG doc embeddings). ADR-001 (mongodb-vs-postgres) states MongoDB is 'the sole database for the application'. The JSON-file flag store and the pgvector store are undocumented deviations from that decision and from copilot-instructions section 3 (which lists only Mongoose models).
evidence: docker-compose.yml postgres service (pgvector/pgvector:pg17) lines 35-45; backend/features.json as flag store; ADR-001 'Use MongoDB ... as the sole database'
recommendation: Either consolidate or, more realistically, supersede/amend ADR-001 with a new ADR documenting the polyglot persistence reality (Mongo for OLTP, file for flags, pgvector for RAG) and the rationale/boundaries for each.

issue: The frontend service sets VITE_API_URL=http://backend:5000, but VITE_API_URL is only read by the Vite DEV server proxy (vite.config.js server.proxy). The production frontend is a static build and never reads env at runtime; all axios calls use relative '/api' paths. In the docker-compose topology the built frontend is served separately on :3000 with no proxy/reverse-proxy to the backend, so relative /api calls will hit the static-file server, not the API. The API base-URL convention is implicit and only works in same-origin (Heroku) or CRA-style dev proxy deployments.
evidence: docker-compose.yml:31 VITE_API_URL; vite.config.js reads it only under server.proxy; no axios baseURL anywhere in frontend/src (grep empty); server.js:40-45 serves frontend/build same-origin only in production
recommendation: Decide and document the frontend->backend addressing convention (same-origin reverse proxy vs build-time injected base URL). Remove the misleading VITE_API_URL from the frontend compose service or add a reverse proxy / build-time API base.

issue: Order and Product models are anaemic: pure schema with no behavior. State transitions (markPaid, markDelivered) and invariants (recompute totals, add review + recompute rating) live in controllers rather than on the models. Combined with the missing service layer, all domain behavior is in HTTP handlers.
evidence: orderModel.js has no instance methods; updateOrderToPaid sets order.isPaid/paidAt/paymentResult in the controller (orderController.js:64-71); rating average computed in productController.js:139
recommendation: Move state transitions and invariant enforcement onto model instance methods or a service. Low priority given project size; tracked as the same root cause as the missing-service-layer finding.

issue: Path coupling / leaky filesystem boundary: the controller resolves the flag file via path.join(process.cwd-ish path.resolve(), 'backend', 'features.json'). This hardcodes the assumption that the process is launched from the repo root, coupling a controller to the deploy layout. The MCP server resolves the SAME file via a different strategy (relative to import.meta.url, ../../backend/features.json). Two components reference one resource through two fragile, divergent path computations.
recommendation: Centralize the flag-store location (single config/env var) and access it through one module. Removes the dual brittle path resolution and the implicit cwd dependency.

issue: Auth/error cross-cutting concern is copy-pasted into every Redux thunk: the 'Not authorized, token failed' string match -> dispatch(logout()) appears in all six order actions and across user/feature actions. The frontend logout trigger is coupled to an exact backend error string (authMiddleware.js:23). Changing that backend message silently breaks auto-logout everywhere. ADR-0001 already flags this brittle coupling.
evidence: Identical catch block with message === 'Not authorized, token failed' repeated at orderActions.js:58,95,140,181,218,255 and featureActions.js:62; backend source string authMiddleware.js:23
recommendation: Centralize in one axios response interceptor that detects 401 and dispatches logout, instead of string-matching in every thunk. Replace string coupling with an HTTP 401 status check.

issue: getUsers (GET /api/users, admin) returns full User documents including the bcrypt password hash; getUserById (line 134) correctly uses .select('-password') but the list endpoint does not. Inconsistent response contract for the same resource across two endpoints, and the list shape leaks a credential field. (Cross-ref security-review HIGH and performance-review PERF-007.)
evidence: userController.js:111 await User.find({}) with no .select('-password'); compare userController.js:134 .select('-password')
recommendation: Standardize the User response projection (exclude password) in one place — a model toJSON transform or a shared serializer — so every endpoint returns the same safe shape. Cross-reference: resolves security data-exposure + perf over-fetch.

issue: Inconsistent list-response contracts across the API. getProducts returns a paginated envelope { products, page, pages } (productController.js:25), while getOrders, getMyOrders, getUsers return bare unbounded arrays with no envelope/pagination. Clients must special-case each list endpoint; adding pagination later to orders/users is a breaking change. (Overlaps performance-review PERF-005/006/007 on unbounded result sets.)
evidence: productController.js:25 res.json({products,page,pages}); orderController.js:106 & 114 res.json(orders); userController.js:112 res.json(users)
recommendation: Adopt one list-response convention (paginated envelope) across all collection endpoints now, before clients depend on the bare-array shape. Document it as an API contract ADR.

issue: The RAG MCP embeds raw SQL (including pgvector operator <=> and ::vector casts) directly in the tool handler with no repository/data-access layer. DB config, connection lifecycle, embedding, and query are all in one function. The pgvector schema (table 'chunks', column names) is referenced by an external embed script (scripts/embed_chunks.js, per the error message) but there is no shared schema/DAL between the indexer and the searcher — the contract is implicit and can drift.
evidence: index.ts:117-128 inline SELECT ... embedding <=> $1::vector FROM chunks; DB_CONFIG inline at index.ts:19-25; per-call new pg.Client at index.ts:131 (also performance-review PERF-001)
recommendation: Extract a small data-access module for the chunks table shared by indexer and searcher (single source of schema truth). Pair with the pooled-connection fix from performance-review. Document the RAG/pgvector subsystem boundary in an ADR.

issue: Both MCP servers duplicate the same boilerplate (server bootstrap, a status resource at server://status, main()/catch pattern) with no shared package. Two independently-evolving copies of the MCP host scaffolding; divergence risk as more tools are added.
evidence: Identical status resource and main() in mcp-server-search-docs/src/index.ts:168-189 and mcp-server-feature-flags/src/index.ts:303-324
recommendation: Extract shared MCP scaffolding into a common internal package or template if more MCP servers are anticipated. Low priority at two servers.

issue: No validation layer at the API boundary. Controllers destructure req.body and pass values straight to Mongoose with no schema validation (registerUser email/password format, addOrderItems numeric prices, updateUser isAdmin coercion). copilot-instructions section 6 explicitly says 'Don't skip request body validation' yet there is no Joi/express-validator anywhere (grep empty). This is an architectural gap (missing validation tier), distinct from the per-field security issues.
evidence: userController.js:9/31 raw destructure; orderController.js:8-16 raw destructure of price fields; no validation dependency in package.json
recommendation: Add a request-validation tier (middleware with Joi/zod schemas per route) as a documented architectural layer between routes and controllers. Cross-ref security-review NoSQL-injection / no-password-strength findings.

issue: Redux store registers 23 reducers in a single combineReducers and the project follows the legacy actions/constants/reducers triad with heavy boilerplate (string constants, manual REQUEST/SUCCESS/FAIL). This is the documented convention (copilot-instructions 5.5, ADR-002 redux-vs-context) so it is NOT a violation, but the per-domain triplication (e.g. the repeated auth-error catch block) is a cohesion smell worth noting for future consolidation.
evidence: store.js:36-60 combineReducers with 23 slices; ADR-002 documents Redux+thunk choice
recommendation: No action required to comply with ADRs. If modernizing later, Redux Toolkit slices would remove the constants/boilerplate. Noted for awareness, not a blocker.

note: ADR-0001 (JWT/localStorage), ADR-0002 (client-trusted PayPal), ADR-0003 (no migration tooling), ADR-001 (MongoDB), ADR-002 (Redux), ADR-003 (JWT vs session), ADR-004 (PayPal vs Stripe), ADR-005 (Bootstrap vs Tailwind) all loaded and cross-referenced. Note: ADR-005 chose Bootstrap but the codebase now uses Tailwind v4 + shadcn/ui (copilot-instructions 2) — ADR-005 is stale/superseded and should be updated, though styling is out of architecture scope.
